name: Momos
subtitle: Steamed dumplings with a juicy filling, eaten with a fiery tomato-chilli chutney

ingredients.note: or finely chopped cabbage for a vegetarian version

prepNotes: Everything in the filling must be chopped very fine and kept raw. It cooks in the steamer, and any large piece will tear the wrapper.
Do not salt the filling until just before you fill: salt draws water out of the cabbage and makes the dough soggy.

steps.text: Knead the flour with water and a pinch of salt into a firm, smooth dough. Rest 30 minutes covered.
Mix the filling ingredients with the oil and pepper. Salt it only when you are ready to fill.
Roll the dough very thin and cut 8cm rounds, keeping the edges thinner than the centre.
steps.tip: Thin edges, thicker middle. Otherwise the pleated top is doughy.

steps.text: Place a spoon of filling in each, then pleat and seal into a half-moon or a gathered purse.
Steam in a greased steamer for 10-12 minutes. The wrappers turn translucent and stop looking floury.
steps.tip: Do not crowd them; they swell and stick together.

steps.text: For the chutney, boil the tomatoes and dried chillies, then blend with garlic and salt. Serve alongside.

storage: Best straight from the steamer. Uncooked momos freeze well on a tray for a month. Steam from frozen, adding 4 minutes. Cooked ones go rubbery.

nutrition.method: Estimated from raw ingredients using USDA FoodData Central. Cooking losses are not modelled and added salt is excluded, so sodium is not given.
nutrition.caveat: Ingredients given to taste rather than by weight are counted as zero, so the real figure is a little higher than this. The + says so.
